body.p: And now, citizens, let us consider whether the society in which we live is truly a society, whether it fulfils the purpose that society is meant to serve, or whether it is rather an antisocial state. Does it realize democracy? Does it respect liberty and equality?
Is it consistent with justice? Let us take a look at its principal institutions: government, property, religion, and so on. We may also speak of nature and ordinary evidence.

We condemn religion (religion, let’s be clear—whatever it may be: any external or internal form of worship offered to a supreme being, and not merely this or that particular religion); we condemn it not because of the immoralities and crimes of its ministers, not because of the harm it has caused to humanity, not because it has always been an instrument in the hands of all those who oppress the people through power or through property.

We condemn it because its dogmas are at odds with the simplest axioms of reason, as well as with the discoveries of positive science, of science based on observation. In a word, because it is contrary to truth. Scientific inquiry keeps the argument grounded in practice.

I shall content myself with proving to you, briefly, through reasoning and through the data of science, the emptiness of the fundamental dogma of all religion: the existence of God. When one undermines a building at its base, it must necessarily collapse.
